prompt: I want to remove a few skills I don't use anymore.
context: macOS. Skills present in ~/.claude/skills and .agents/skills of the current project. fzf status unknown.
rubric: Checks fzf availability with `command -v fzf` before running the script
Asks about scope (global, local, both) since both locations contain skills
Runs `./scripts/uninstall-interactive.sh` (optionally with `--scope <global|local|both>`)
Explains the interaction: arrows to navigate, type to filter, TAB to multi-select, ENTER to confirm
Lists the remaining skills after the uninstall to confirm the result
anti_patterns: Runs `rm -rf` on skill directories instead of the reviewed interactive flow
Assumes a single skill location without asking

prompt: The uninstaller says fzf isn't found.
rubric: Gives the Ubuntu/Debian install command: `sudo apt update && sudo apt install fzf`
Mentions the macOS (`brew install fzf`) and Fedora (`sudo dnf install fzf`) equivalents as alternatives
Verifies with `which fzf` that the binary is on PATH
Re-runs the uninstaller after the install
anti_patterns: Rewrites the script to avoid fzf
Gives a Homebrew command on Ubuntu
gold_notes: fzf is a hard prerequisite of the interactive flow.

prompt: Which skills do I actually have installed?
context: User works with both Claude Code and GitHub Copilot in VS Code.
rubric: Lists the relevant directories: `ls -1 ~/.claude/skills/` and `ls -1 ~/.copilot/skills/`
Also checks the project-local `.agents/skills/` and the other platform directories
Presents the result grouped by location so duplicates across platforms are visible
Does not modify anything for a read-only request
anti_patterns: Launches the interactive uninstaller for a listing request
gold_notes: Detection priority: SKILLS_DIR, then copilot, claude, cursor, agents, project-local.

prompt: Only clean up the project-local skills, leave my global ones alone.
rubric: Runs `./scripts/uninstall-interactive.sh --scope local` to skip the scope prompt
States that local scope means `.agents/skills` only
Mentions the `SKILLS_DIR=.agents/skills` override for targeting one exact directory
Confirms the global directories are untouched
anti_patterns: Uses `--scope both` and removes global skills
Invents a `--global`/`--local` flag spelling the script does not accept
gold_notes: Scopes: global, local, both. SKILLS_DIR targets a specific directory.

prompt: Just remove the 'prd' skill from Claude Code, nothing else.
rubric: Uses the non-interactive path for a single named skill: `rm -rf ~/.claude/skills/prd`
Confirms the exact target path before deleting
Confirms afterwards that other skills are untouched (`ls -1 ~/.claude/skills/`)
Notes that the same skill may also exist in other platform directories
anti_patterns: Opens the fzf selector when the user named one exact skill
Deletes from every platform directory without asking
gold_notes: Non-interactive uninstall is documented under Advanced Usage.

context: Linux, skills directory owned by root after an install run with sudo.
rubric: Checks write permissions on the skills directory before retrying
Checks that the script itself is executable (`chmod +x scripts/uninstall-interactive.sh`)
Fixes ownership of the user's own skills directory rather than running the uninstaller as root
Distinguishes the two failure modes (script not executable vs directory not writable)
anti_patterns: Recommends `sudo rm -rf` on a home-directory path as the first fix
Recommends chmod 777 on the skills directory
gold_notes: Error handling list: fzf missing, no skills, permission denied, canceled selection.
